$comment: Provenance is written by hand. Sizes and SHA-256 sums are generated into manifest.json by scripts/build_manifest.py and must never be edited here. `collection` says which body of work a file belongs to; `stage` says whether the file is a third-party input (`original`) or something this project derived from one (`converted`). `modified_from_supplied` is set when an `original` artifact is not byte-identical to what the supplier sent, and says exactly what was changed; the SHA-256 then records our copy and cannot be checked against the supplier's. The two are separate axes, so a request for the converted GIAMIP data can be expressed. `permission` records whether the supplier has agreed to redistribution through https://data.gadopt.org/giamip/: one of `granted`, `requested`, `not_asked`. An artifact whose permission is not `granted` is never uploaded and is never fetched. A `converted` artifact is a file this project wrote from the originals: it lists them in `derived_from` and names its `converter`, its permission follows theirs, and scripts/build_manifest.py gives it an `object` key, versions/<sha256>/<path>, so every version keeps its own object on the store.

giamip/ice-history.zip.description: Six global ice-thickness histories interpolated onto the prescribed Gauss-Legendre grid: ICE-6G_D, ICE-7G_NA, PaleoMIST 1a and GLAC3c profiles 1, 2 and 3.
giamip/ice-history.zip.source_citation: GIAMIP input distribution. The underlying reconstructions are third-party and each carries its own terms: ICE-6G_D (Peltier, Argus and Drummond), ICE-7G_NA (Roy and Peltier), PaleoMIST (Gowan et al. 2021), GLAC3 (Tarasov, unpublished).
giamip/ice-history.zip.supplier: GIAMIP organisers, through the shared input folder
giamip/ice-history.zip.notes: The protocol table names GLAC3b; the filenames say GLAC3c_profile; the internal title and source attributes say GLAC3c_merge. All six files declare _FillValue = 0.0 on ice_thickness. PaleoMIST starts at 80 ka with 379 steps; the other five start at 122 ka with 463. Redistribution through https://data.gadopt.org/giamip/ is granted by Sia Ghelichkhani's decision of 2026-09-15.

giamip/initial-topography.zip.description: Three present-day bed elevations on the prescribed grid, differing only in the Antarctic source: BedMachine Antarctica v3, Bedmap3 or Bedmap2, each merged with BedMachine Greenland v5.5 and GEBCO.
giamip/initial-topography.zip.source_citation: GIAMIP input distribution. Fretwell et al. (2013) Bedmap2; Pritchard et al. (2025) Bedmap3; Morlighem et al. (2020) BedMachine; GEBCO.
giamip/initial-topography.zip.supplier: GIAMIP organisers, through the shared input folder
giamip/initial-topography.zip.notes: The source attribute of the BedMachine Antarctica v3 file names BedMachine Greenland twice and never names its Antarctic dataset. The other two files are correct. All three reference a grid_mapping variable named crs that does not exist in the file. Redistribution through https://data.gadopt.org/giamip/ is granted by Sia Ghelichkhani's decision of 2026-09-15.
